attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated as his thesis.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense assertion. The normalisation keeps the OpenAI/Anthropic exclusion and the trillion-dollar benchmark. 'Or more' is dropped, which is a minor loss.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: demand from outside the two labs is too small to justify the capex. The result still depends on assumptions the speaker never supplied: asset life, returns, where the exclusion boundary sits, and how the capex is defined.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure: over 20M paid Copilot seats in the target quarter. This shows paid adoption outside the labs, but it gives no revenue, so it can't be compared with the capex.
Google's own disclosure: about 800% growth in gen-AI product revenue. There is no absolute base and no breakdown by customer, so it can't settle sufficiency.
An earlier quarter's figure (OpenAI about 45% of Microsoft's RPO), covering all commercial backlog. It describes concentration but is not AI demand excluding the labs.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows real paid AI adoption outside the two labs (Copilot seats, Google's gen-AI revenue growth). It gives no absolute figure for non-lab demand and no model of what level would justify a trillion dollars of capex. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition can be established.

attribution.note: His own words, framed as a personal view.

semantics.note: A causal explanation explicitly hedged as personal belief ('I personally think'), comparable to 'I suspect'. 'Peculiar' has no defined meaning, so there is nothing testable to score.

contract.note: The contract correctly recognises that no support or contradiction condition can be set without replacing 'peculiar' with an allegation the evaluator chooses.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1, dated before the cutoff, sets out its run-rate method (28 days ×13 plus subscriptions ×12). It neither confirms nor refutes any 'peculiar' practice.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged personal suspicion about an undefined 'peculiar' calculation practice. Under policy, hedged and untestable causal claims are not scored. The disclosed methodology matches the reported method but cannot test an unspecified allegation.

attribution.note: His own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The 'if' frames the greed charge. The factual parts (continued customer intake while availability struggled around 99%) are asserted as observations. Greed is evaluative and correctly left out.

contract.note: The reading is fair. The April-only window is the evaluator's convention: the speaker gave no window, and a rolling figure could also fairly test 'struggles to keep above two nines'. That choice affects the result.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure of capacity expansion and a growing customer base in April. It partly supports intake and capacity pressure but gives no uptime figure. The quoted excerpt does not show the reliability strain the drafter describes.
Anthropic's own disclosure: customers spending over $1M doubled to more than 1,000. This partly supports continued customer growth, but cohort growth is not the same as new intake.
The Register reports 90-day Claude.ai uptime of 98.82% as of April 6, plus demand strain. It is a rolling window covering one service, not April monthly uptime.

reviews.rationale: Capacity pressure and continued customer growth are reasonably supported by Anthropic's disclosures and The Register. The availability element is not established for April under the contract: the only figure is a 90-day rolling reading for Claude.ai, and the April status data was not recovered. The claim as a whole is unresolved.

attribution.note: His own words. He repeats the point firmly nearby ('these companies will not die').

semantics.note: A conditional forecast whose antecedent is the bubble bursting. The firm restatement ('will not die') makes it a committed forecast. It names no horizon.

contract.note: Reading 'die' as failure of the operating business is ordinary and fair. 'Bubble bursting' has no threshold, and no survival interval after a collapse is given.

evidence.note: A Kiplinger analysis dated on the evaluation date describes the market as late cycle, not a confirmed peak. It does not show that the antecedent has occurred.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent (an AI bubble collapse) is unknown, there is no deadline, and the packet shows no failure of a named company. Policy does not score a conditional whose antecedent is unknown, and continued survival cannot conclusively support a forecast with no deadline.
